findings.title: Cascade: Memory exhaustion from unbounded response body conversion in bot detection
findings.description: Both looksLikeBotProtection and looksLikeGenericError convert the entire response body to lowercase string without size constraints. While readResponseBody limits reads to 10MB, a malicious/broken Yad2 server can send exactly 10MB of data. Each bot detection check allocates a new 10MB lowercase string (20MB total per non-200 response). Under concurrent enrichment (MaxConcurrentFetches=4 default), four simultaneous bot-challenged item fetches allocate 80MB immediately. If the scheduler is under memory pressure or running on constrained hardware, this triggers OOM or significant GC pauses, cascading into context deadline exceeded errors on other inflight requests.
evidence: yad2.go:242-249: looksLikeBotProtection calls strings.ToLower(string(body)) on full body
yad2.go:236-239: looksLikeGenericError calls strings.ToLower(string(body)) on full body
yad2.go:104: looksLikeBotProtection called on non-200 status before checking size
yad2.go:107: looksLikeGenericError called on 400 status before checking size
yad2.go:21: maxResponseSize = 10 * 1024 * 1024 allows 10MB reads
scheduler.go:563-567: concurrency defaults to 4 when MaxConcurrentFetches <= 0
scheduler.go:676: enrichment runs with 25-minute timeout, allowing many concurrent item fetches

attack_scenario.trigger: Yad2 serves 10MB HTML error pages (CDN misconfiguration, attack proxy, or legitimate large error page with embedded diagnostics)
steps: Scheduler initiates 4 concurrent processGroup calls
Each group fetches listings successfully, then enriches 5 items (defaultMaxPerCycle)
Yad2 item endpoint returns 403 with 10MB body for all enrichment requests
FetchItem calls looksLikeBotProtection: allocates 10MB + 10MB lowercase = 20MB per call
4 groups × 5 items × 20MB = 400MB allocated within seconds
Go GC struggles, stop-the-world pauses block all goroutines
kmEnrichTimeout (25 min) prevents early abort, memory pressure continues
Other HTTP requests timeout waiting for GC, ErrChallenge propagates, backoff doubles
Next cycle repeats with 2× interval, but same memory pattern if errors persist
attack_scenario.outcome: Service degradation or OOM crash. Even if not fatal, GC pauses cause listing page fetches to timeout, triggering unnecessary backoff escalation.

findings.title: Assumption violation: looksLikeBotProtection false positive on legitimate user-generated content
findings.description: looksLikeBotProtection matches 'captcha' and 'are you for real' in lowercase body text. If Yad2's listing page contains user-generated content (seller description, comments, embedded reviews) mentioning these strings, FetchItem returns ErrChallenge. Enricher immediately aborts enrichment for ALL remaining items in the batch, even though the 'challenge' was a false positive. This is permanent: the same listing will trigger the false positive on every cycle, preventing enrichment of subsequent listings indefinitely.
evidence: yad2.go:249: checks strings.Contains(h, 'captcha') on full body
yad2.go:247: checks strings.Contains(h, 'are you for real') on full body
yad2.go:104-105: FetchItem returns ErrChallenge on looksLikeBotProtection match
enricher.go:85-90: on ErrChallenge, Enrich() immediately returns without processing remaining items
enricher.go:52-66: items are processed sequentially; false positive on index N skips N+1..end forever

attack_scenario.trigger: Listing page contains user text: 'This car is amazing, are you for real asking only 50k?' or 'Includes captcha-enabled dash cam'
steps: Enricher.Enrich processes 10 listings needing km data
Listing at index 3 has token 'xyz-123', page contains seller comment with trigger phrase
FetchItem('xyz-123') receives 200 OK with legitimate HTML
looksLikeBotProtection scans full body, matches 'are you for real' in seller comment
FetchItem returns ErrChallenge
Enrich() logs 'enrichment blocked by anti-bot protection' and returns immediately
Listings 4-10 remain unenriched (Km=0, ImageURL='', City='')
Next cycle: same listing order, same false positive, same abort
User never receives enriched data for 70% of listings
attack_scenario.outcome: Permanent enrichment failure for all listings after the false-positive listing. Users receive incomplete notifications (missing km/city/image), reducing trust and utility.

findings.title: Composition failure: itemClient shares proxy with listing client, negating isolation intent
findings.description: The change introduces itemClient to isolate item-page cookies from listing-page cookies. However, both clients are initialized with the same proxy in NewFetcher and NewFetcherWithProxyPool. From Yad2's perspective, both clients originate from the same IP. If itemClient triggers bot detection (429, captcha challenge), Yad2 likely flags the IP, not just the cookie jar. Subsequent listing fetches from client (same IP) will also be challenged, despite separate cookie jars. The isolation provides no defense if bot detection is IP-based.
evidence: yad2.go:34-44: NewFetcher passes same 'proxy' param to both NewClient calls
yad2.go:47-73: NewFetcherWithProxyPool calls pool.Next() once, uses same proxy for both clients
yad2.go:25-26: comment claims 'isolated cookie jar' but doesn't mention IP sharing
enricher.go:83: FetchItem uses itemClient for all item fetches
scheduler.go:661: activeFetcher (using 'client') fetches listings after enrichment

attack_scenario.trigger: Yad2 implements IP-based rate limiting or bot detection (common CDN behavior)
steps: Scheduler creates Yad2Fetcher with proxy P1 (IP 203.0.113.5)
Both client and itemClient use proxy P1
Group fetch: client fetches listing page via P1 successfully
Enrichment: itemClient fetches 5 item pages rapidly (2s delay × 5 = 10s total)
Yad2 CDN flags IP 203.0.113.5 for aggressive scraping (5 item reqs in 10s)
Next listing fetch from client (still using P1) receives 403 with bot challenge
Fetch fails, ErrChallenge propagates, backoff doubles
Next cycle uses same proxy (pool.Next() may return P1 again), same IP, same block
attack_scenario.outcome: Cookie isolation provides no protection. Proxy gets burned by enrichment, listing fetches fail. Intended benefit of separating clients is not realized.

findings.title: Abuse case: Alternating success/failure bypasses consecutive failure abort, polluting enrichment indefinitely
findings.description: Consecutive failure counter resets to 0 on any success. An attacker or flaky network can serve: fail, fail, success (counter→0), fail, fail, success (counter→0), repeating. Enrichment never aborts (counter never reaches 3), but data is heavily polluted: every third item succeeds with potentially manipulated km/city data, others fail silently. The enrichment loop runs to completion (or MaxPerCycle limit), wasting time and storing bad data without operator visibility.
evidence: enricher.go:108: consecutiveFailures = 0 on any successful FetchItem
enricher.go:97-104: abort only when consecutiveFailures >= 3
enricher.go:92: consecutiveFailures++ on non-ErrChallenge errors
enricher_test.go:372-405: TestEnricher_ConsecutiveFailureResets validates this exact behavior

attack_scenario.trigger: Malicious proxy alternates between serving real Yad2 responses and injected fake responses, or flaky network has 66% failure rate
steps: Enricher processes 15 listings
Item 0: HTTP timeout → consecutiveFailures=1
Item 1: 500 error → consecutiveFailures=2
Item 2: Success (attacker injects km=1, city='fake') → consecutiveFailures=0, enriched=1
Item 3: timeout → consecutiveFailures=1
Item 4: 500 → consecutiveFailures=2
Item 5: Success (fake data) → consecutiveFailures=0, enriched=2
Pattern repeats for all 15 items
Enrich() returns enriched=5, no abort, 10 items unenriched but no error logged at summary level
attack_scenario.outcome: Database contains 5 listings with manipulated km/city (pricing/filtering broken). 10 listings remain unenriched (Km=0) but user doesn't know why. No clear signal that enrichment is compromised.

findings.title: Timing assumption: looksLikeGenericError only checks 400, but 403 title check is dead code
findings.description: looksLikeGenericError checks for both '<title>400 bad request</title>' and '<title>403 forbidden</title>', but FetchItem only calls it when StatusCode == 400. The 403 check is unreachable. If Yad2's nginx/CDN returns a generic 403 page (not matching looksLikeBotProtection patterns), FetchItem skips looksLikeGenericError, returns a generic status error (not ErrChallenge), increments consecutiveFailures instead of aborting immediately. Enrichment continues unnecessarily, burning through MaxPerCycle budget on predictable 403 failures.
evidence: yad2.go:236-239: looksLikeGenericError checks both 400 and 403 titles
yad2.go:107-109: looksLikeGenericError called ONLY when result.StatusCode == http.StatusBadRequest (400)
yad2.go:104-106: 403 with looksLikeBotProtection → ErrChallenge, but generic 403 → falls through to line 119

attack_scenario.trigger: Yad2 CDN serves generic '<title>403 Forbidden</title>' without perfdrive/shieldsquare markers (e.g., IP blocklist, geo-restriction)
steps: Enricher starts with 10 items
Item 0: FetchItem receives 403 with body '<html><title>403 Forbidden</title></html>'
looksLikeBotProtection scans body, no 'perfdrive'/'captcha' match → returns false
StatusCode != 400, so looksLikeGenericError not called
Falls through to line 119: returns generic 'status 403' error (not ErrChallenge)
Enricher increments consecutiveFailures=1, continues
Items 1-2: same 403, consecutiveFailures=2, 3
Item 3: consecutiveFailures=3, abort
Items 4-10 skipped, but enrichment ran 3 unnecessary HTTP requests when abort-on-first would suffice
attack_scenario.outcome: Wastes 3 attempts on predictable generic 403s instead of immediate abort. Not critical but inefficient.

findings.title: Cascade: defaultMaxPerCycle=5 + defaultEnrichDelay=2s enables rapid proxy burnout under concurrent groups
findings.description: Each CanonicalGroup runs concurrently (default 4 groups). Each group enriches up to 5 items with 2s delay = 10 seconds total per group. With 4 groups in parallel, itemClient makes 20 item requests in ~10 seconds (ignoring network latency). If all groups share the same itemClient instance (which they do—Yad2Fetcher is reused per source), Yad2 sees 20 item requests from the same IP in 10s. Most anti-scraping systems flag >10 req/min from single IP. This triggers IP-based rate limiting, returns 429/403 for subsequent requests. Once IP is flagged, both itemClient AND client (listing fetches) fail for all groups. Backoff escalates, but IP remains burned. Proxy rotation doesn't help if proxyPool is small or nil.
evidence: enricher.go:14: defaultEnrichDelay = 2 * time.Second
enricher.go:15: defaultMaxPerCycle = 5
scheduler.go:563-567: concurrency defaults to 4 (MaxConcurrentFetches)
scheduler.go:586-619: each group runs in separate goroutine, all call s.kmEnricher.Enrich
scheduler.go:280-286: fetcherForSource returns same f.fetcher instance for all 'yad2' groups
yad2.go:24-31: single Yad2Fetcher with one itemClient shared across all groups

attack_scenario.trigger: Scheduler has 4 active searches grouped into 4 CanonicalGroups, each returns 10 listings needing enrichment, Yad2 rate limit is 10 req/min per IP
steps: runFetchGroups spawns 4 goroutines (groups A,B,C,D)
T+0s: Group A starts enrichment, sends item request 1 via itemClient
T+0s: Groups B,C,D also start, send requests 2,3,4 simultaneously
T+2s: Groups send requests 5,6,7,8 (after 2s delay)
T+4s: requests 9,10,11,12
T+6s: requests 13,14,15,16
T+8s: requests 17,18,19,20
Yad2 CDN counts 20 requests from IP in 8 seconds → rate limit triggered
T+10s: Next item request from any group receives 429 Too Many Requests
looksLikeBotProtection doesn't match '429' or 'rate limit' → generic error
consecutiveFailures increments across groups (if they share counter) OR each group independently fails 3× and aborts
Either way, all groups fail, backoff doubles, proxy is unusable for next cycle
attack_scenario.outcome: All enrichment fails after 8-10 seconds due to concurrent group saturation. Listings lack km/city/image data. Backoff doubles unnecessarily (not a true bot challenge, just rate limiting). If proxyPool is nil or exhausted, service is degraded for 2× interval.

residual_risks.description: If Yad2 changes error page format (removes 'perfdrive' markers, adds new anti-bot vendor), looksLikeBotProtection and looksLikeGenericError will fail to detect challenges. Enrichment will treat bot pages as parse errors, logging 'parse item: unexpected JSON' instead of aborting. This burns through MaxPerCycle budget and proxy quota without clear error signal.
residual_risks.mitigation: None in current code. Detection is heuristic-based, no fallback or monitoring for parse errors that might indicate undetected challenges.

residual_risks.description: kmEnrichTimeout is 25 minutes, but MaxPerCycle=5 with 2s delay = only 10 seconds of work. Timeout is 150× longer than expected duration. If enrichment hangs (slow network, proxy blackhole), context won't cancel for 25 minutes. This blocks the scheduler goroutine and prevents other groups from completing within the polling interval.
residual_risks.mitigation: None. Timeout is not per-item, it's for the entire Enrich() call. A single hanging item fetch can block all subsequent enrichment.

testing_gaps.description: No test validates looksLikeBotProtection behavior with 10MB response body. Existing tests use small HTML snippets. Missing coverage for memory allocation and GC impact under realistic maxResponseSize payloads.
testing_gaps.suggested_test: TestLooksLikeBotProtection_LargeBody: construct 10MB HTML with 'captcha' at offset 9MB, measure memory allocation and duration

testing_gaps.description: No test validates concurrent enrichment across multiple groups. TestEnricher tests run sequentially on single Enricher. Missing coverage for shared itemClient under concurrent load.
testing_gaps.suggested_test: TestEnricher_ConcurrentGroups: spawn 4 goroutines each calling Enrich(), measure total request rate and verify rate-limiting behavior

testing_gaps.description: No test validates false positive scenario where legitimate listing page contains 'captcha' or 'are you for real' in user-generated content. looksLikeBotProtection should only match in <head> or <script> context, not in article text.
testing_gaps.suggested_test: TestFetchItem_FalsePositiveCaptchaInContent: serve 200 OK with valid item JSON but seller comment containing 'captcha', verify FetchItem succeeds (not ErrChallenge)

testing_gaps.description: No test validates that generic 403 (without bot-protection markers) is handled correctly. TestYad2Fetcher_Fetch_Non200 only tests Fetch(), not FetchItem(), and doesn't verify ErrChallenge vs generic error.
testing_gaps.suggested_test: TestFetchItem_Generic403: serve '<title>403 Forbidden</title>' without perfdrive, verify error is NOT ErrChallenge
